alignments.note: The ASV writes one English word for the adjacent μὲν οὖν, so rule 70 gives it to one particle and empties the other. *Howbeit* is adversative and answers to the μέν … δέ correlation this verse writes out, so it goes here; giving it to οὖν instead remains defensible.
Second member of the μὲν οὖν pair, left empty under rule 70 since the ASV wrote only one word.
Finite verb. The supplied complementizers go to the infinitival complements they introduce under rule 85, not to this verb.
Infinitive expanded into a finite clause; it keeps the supplied *that* under rule 85 and the *in charge* that completes the ASV's rendering of τηρέω, headed on *kept*.
Reflexive rendered by the two-word emphatic; rule 107's reasoning heads it on the *-self* word.
Infinitive with the supplied *that* under rule 85 and the copular auxiliary; head on *about*, the word carrying μέλλω's sense.
ἐν τάχει rendered by one English adverb; rule 93 makes it one aligned unit headed on the noun and refuses to leave ἐν unrepresented.

*thither* is the ASV's own supplied resumption of Caesarea, whose Greek εἰς Καισάρειαν is already spent on *at Caesarea*; rule 103 makes such supplied content added, and the ASV's own addition markup corroborates. Reading it as a discontinuous second realization of Καισάρειαν under rule 15 remains defensible.

review_notes: The two supplied *that*s go to the infinitives under rule 85 rather than to ἀπεκρίθη.
The μὲν οὖν assignment is the one genuinely open call here; the note records the competing reading.
